shared_elements: elaborate multi-band headdress above the face
circular disc ornament on the chest/pectoral
arms held symmetrically at the sides/front
low-relief geometric ornament panels flanking the body
bilateral symmetry about a vertical axis
justification: Both depict a single frontal, bilaterally symmetrical anthropomorphic personage filling the field, wearing a tall banded headdress over the face and a prominent circular disc ornament on the chest, with arms/ornaments arranged symmetrically and rendered in flat, schematic, block-like relief with strong outlines and geometric infill. The chief difference is that A's carving wraps a three-dimensional bulky body with only a few large sparse motifs (disc, ovals, curved bands) and no accompanying panels, while B is a flat field crowded with an elongated figure surrounded by dense rectilinear sign-like panels at the sides and base.
